thread:
PagerBot: PAGER: on-call page for service=redwood-inferpool-usw, severity=sev2 — node heartbeat missing for node=infer-usw-42 (detected 00:02m ago)
Maya: seeing the page, joining. node shows NotReady in k8s UI.
Alex: pinging infra metrics — node `infer-usw-42` heartbeat gap + kubelet restart spikes at 03:23 UTC.
Jamal: I can repro in logs: `journalctl -u kubelet` shows repeated `kubelet: task reassigned after runtime failure` then `systemd: kubelet.service: main process exited, code=exited`
Maya: can someone paste `kubectl get nodes infer-usw-42 -o wide`?
Alex: ```
NAME           STATUS     ROLES   AGE   VERSION
infer-usw-42   NotReady   <none>  58d   v1.27.3
```
Jen: checking GPU driver logs — found repeated Xid errors around the same time: `NVRM: Xid (0001:86): 79, PID 1245` — looks like GPU driver/kernel OOMs triggering container runtime instability.
Maya: customer traffic routing shows 6% of inference requests retried/failing for a subset of customers pinned to this pool. Support-Rita, can you confirm impacted customers?
Support-Rita: pulled support dashboard — 3 customers with elevated 5xxs (client ids s-211, s-322, s-410). Not high volume overall but some SLAs impacted. Notified account owners.
Jamal: we should cordon and drain the node to stop new pods landing and evict inference pods to healthy nodes. I can run cordon first.
Maya: +1. Also enable temporary autoscale on the dedicated pool to absorb evicted pods — Alex please bump replica count for the inference deployment.
Alex: scaling rr-infer-deploy to 10 -> 16 replicas now. pods will reschedule to other nodes with GPU capacity.
InfraBot: quickcheck: available GPUs in pool=2 nodes with free slots, some pods may queue.
Jamal: cordon done: `kubectl cordon infer-usw-42` -> node is unschedulable. Now draining (graceful): `kubectl drain infer-usw-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force`
Maya: drain in progress, watching for stuck pods (eviction timeout). If container runtime flaps during eviction, we may need node reboot or kubelet restart.
Alex: eviction succeeded for 8/10 pods, 2 pods stuck in Terminating due to containerd not responding. Trying `crictl ps` against node via ssh.
Jamal: on ssh: `systemctl status docker` shows docker/containerd in a crashloop, kernel messages show GPU driver resets. I'm going to recycle the node via cordon->drain->reboot.
Maya: agree. Rebooting node now. Jamal: please run `sudo reboot` and I'll start traffic steering to other regions if we see latency spikes.
Jamal: reboot issued. kernel logs pre-reboot: ```
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (0001:86): 79, PID 1245
[  123.457001] nvidia: GPU has fallen off the bus
[  123.457100] kernel: watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 23s
```
InfraBot: node infer-usw-42 has entered reboot cycle. kubelet last seen 03:23:17 UTC.
Maya: customer impact estimate: ~2% of total inference qps, 3 specific accounts with transient 5xxs. Support-Rita: add short note to those accounts, status page update?
Support-Rita: posting incident update now: "Investigation: GPU driver instability caused node heartbeat loss affecting a small percentage of inference traffic. Mitigation started, evictions underway." :loud_sound:
Alex: nodes in pool rerouted, replica scale is absorbing traffic. Latency for routed requests is steady for most customers, a few retries for pinned folks.
Jamal: node is back reachable on ssh after reboot, but kubelet still flapping — logs show kubelet failing to start due to container runtime socket timeout. Restarting containerd and then kubelet.
Maya: command sequence?
Jamal: `sudo systemctl restart containerd && sudo systemctl restart kubelet` — containerd restarts cleanly now, kubelet comes up, node Ready at 03:39 UTC.
Alex: `kubectl get nodes` now shows infer-usw-42 Ready, pods rescheduled back, no OOMs in the last 5m.
Maya: I'm going to keep monitors at high sensitivity for 30m and leave autoscale elevated for 20m to avoid pressure.
InfraBot: autoscale revert scheduled in 20m.
Jamal: follow-up actions: 1) isolate GPU driver version on that AMI and mark for repro test; 2) add kubelet restart-on-failure mitigation script to drain earlier; 3) run mem/gpu stress test on node image in canary.
Maya: logging action items: assign to Jamal for driver repro (P0), Alex for autoscale playbook tweak (P1), Jen for kernel/gpu telemetry correlation (P1).
Support-Rita: sent customers final update: short impact, mitigation complete, follow-up investigation ongoing.
Maya: thanks everyone. I'll sign off after 30m stable. :thumbsup:
PagerBot: INCIDENT: sev2 resolved — monitor-only. Close on-call if no further pages in 30m.
